summary: A news-style article describes a predicted series of powerful solar tsunamis (Moreton waves) heading for Earth, first detected on September 10, 2023. It covers scientists' warnings of a potential global electromagnetic blackout, public panic, worldwide drills, shelters, aviation and satellite risks, the "Project Helioshield" initiative, and market turmoil, ending on a note of cautious hope.
one_line: Scientists warn of unprecedented solar tsunamis threatening Earth's grids, satellites, aviation and markets, prompting global drills, panic, and the Project Helioshield magnetic shield initiative.
key_facts: Dr. Evelyn Solaris, an astrophysicist at the International Space Weather Institute, first noticed anomalous helioseismometer readings on September 10, 2023.
Solar tsunamis, scientifically called Moreton waves, form when solar flares release energy equivalent to millions of hydrogen bombs and send hot plasma rippling across the sun's surface.
At a press conference on September 30, 2023, Dr. Evelyn Solaris said the issue is "not a question of 'if' but 'when'."

Professor Raymond Blackwood of the University of New Horizons warned on October 3, 2023 that every electrical grid worldwide could short out simultaneously, disabling communications, banking, transportation and utilities.
Panic has spread, with grocery stores running out of supplies and families stockpiling essentials; the article compares it to the days before Y2K, on a grander scale.
On November 5, 2023, at 8:43 PM GMT, worldwide simulation exercises began, including cities shutting down power grids and testing emergency broadcast systems.
In New York City, underground bunkers were repurposed as emergency shelters with Faraday cages to protect electronics.
China put its recently completed Disaster Mitigation Space Station into full operational mode to monitor and mitigate the solar storm's effects.

Aviation analyst Katherine Vega, a former airline pilot, told the International Civil Aviation Organization that airlines should ground flights when the first wave hits because GPS signals could be disrupted.
Satellite operators and agencies are planning to shift critical operations to more protected orbital slots and ready replacement satellites.
On November 20, 2023, "Project Helioshield" was unveiled, led by Jonathan Thorne, aiming to deploy satellites creating a magnetic shield around Earth.
Stock markets have plummeted; financial analyst Laura Chen urged calm in a New York Times op-ed, saying markets rebound robustly after uncertainty.
